title: Rees deformation functoriality and the fixed-scheme inclusion
statement:
Let $X,X'$ be separated finite-type schemes over the algebraically closed field $k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be closed subschemes with ideals $I,J$, and let $f:X'\to X$ be a $k$-morphism satisfying $f^{\cdot}I\,\mathcal O_{X'}\subseteq J$. Put $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$ as in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Define the Rees deformation by
$$\widetilde X_Z=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{X_D}\bigl(\mathcal O_{X_D}[I/t]\bigr),$$
where the algebra is the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_{X_D}[t^{-1}]$ generated by $I/t$; define $\widetilde X'_{Z'}$ similarly. Its generic fibre is $X_\eta$, its special fibre is the normal cone $N_{Z/X}$ of [pur9-def-normal-cone], and the augmentation gives a closed zero section $Z_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde X_Z$. These are separated finite-type lifts. The map $f$ induces a unique lift $\widetilde f:\widetilde X'_{Z'}\to\widetilde X_Z$ over $f_D$. Its special fibre is the graded map $N_{Z'/X'}\to N_{Z/X}$ induced by $f^{\cdot}$.

The image of that special-fibre map is set-theoretically supported on the zero section if and only if $(f^{\cdot}I)^r\mathcal O_{X'}\subseteq J^{r+1}$ for some $r\geq1$. If $Z'=f^{-1}Z$ scheme-theoretically, the induced map $\widetilde X'_{Z'}\to\widetilde X_Z\times_X X'$ is a closed immersion, and the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the zero section under the special-fibre map is exactly $Z'$.

For any separated finite-type $k$-scheme $C$ and $k$-morphism $c:C\to X\times_kX$ (the geometric correspondence data of [def-trf-correspondence]), put $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ and let $d:F\to X$ be the fixed-scheme projection of [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Applying the preceding construction to $c:C\to X\times_kX$ and the closed pair $Z\times Z\hookrightarrow X\times_kX$ gives the lifted correspondence
$$\widetilde c:\widetilde C_{c^{-1}(Z\times Z)}\longrightarrow\widetilde X_Z\times_D\widetilde X_Z.$$
Writing $Z_F=d^{-1}(Z)$ and applying the same Rees construction to the closed pair $Z_F\hookrightarrow F$, the fixed-square relation gives a natural closed immersion
$$\widetilde F_{Z_F}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c).$$
Here $\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$ is the fibre product of $\widetilde c$ and the relative diagonal of $\widetilde X_Z$ over $D$. On generic fibres this is the canonical identification with $\operatorname{Fix}(c)_\eta=F\times_k\eta$.

proof.text: Work first on $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, with ideal $I_U\subset A$. Before localizing the parameter, write $E(A,I_U)=A[t,I_U/t]\subset A[t,t^{-1}]$. The coefficient of $t^m$ lies in $A$ for $m\ge0$ and in $I_U^{-m}$ for $m<0$. Indeed products of generators have this property; conversely $I_U^n$ consists of finite sums of products of $n$ elements of $I_U$, so $a t^{-n}$ is a sum of products of $a_i/t$. Thus, with $H_m=A$ for $m\ge0$ and $H_{-n}=I_U^n$ for $n>0$, the additive decomposition is $E(A,I_U)=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbf Z}H_m t^m$, with multiplication inherited from Laurent polynomials. Restriction to a principal open $A\to A_s$ gives $E(A,I_U)_s=E(A_s,I_UA_s)$: each localized degree-$m$ coefficient is $(H_m)_s$ by localization of ideal powers [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and a finite Laurent sum with coefficients $b_m/s^{e_m}$ is the image of $(\sum_m b_m s^{e-e_m}t^m)/s^e$ with $e=\max_m e_m$.

source.place: Notation 1.4.1(a); expanded affine algebra calculation; Stacks 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme), ideal products and powers

proof.text: Put $R=k[t]_{(t)}$ and $S=k[t]\setminus(t)$. On $U_D$ the algebra in the statement is $Q(A,I_U)=S^{-1}E(A,I_U)$, regarded as an $A\otimes_kR$-algebra. Step 1 identifies its restrictions on all principal opens of $U$, and the same holds after localizing at any $g\in A\otimes_kR$: localizing the subalgebra generated by $I_U/t$ generates exactly the localized ideal divided by $t$, with fractions witnessed in the localized Laurent ring. Hence the given subalgebra sheaf is locally the module sheaf associated to $Q(A,I_U)$; it is quasi-coherent by the affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2)--(4) to form its relative spectrum and identify its affine charts with $\operatorname{Spec}Q(A,I_U)$. This proves that the displayed formula defines an affine $X_D$-scheme with the asserted projection, and justifies checking subsequent algebra maps and identities on these charts.

Inverting $t$ in $E(A,I_U)$ gives $A[t,t^{-1}]$, since every extra generator $a/t$ already lies there. After localizing by $S$ this is $A\otimes_k k(t)$, so the generic fibre is $U_\eta$. For the special fibre, the degree-$m$ component of $tE$ is $H_{m-1}t^m$. Consequently $E/tE$ has degree zero $A/I_U$, degree $-n$ equal to $I_U^n/I_U^{n+1}$ for $n>0$, and zero in positive degrees. Multiplication is $[a]_n[b]_r=[ab]_{n+r}$. Every $s\in S$ reduces to the nonzero scalar $s(0)$, so localizing by $S$ does not change this quotient. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] therefore gives the special fibre $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{gr}_{I_U}A$. The restriction-compatible affine description in [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] and the definition [pur9-def-normal-cone] identify these charts, with their projections, with $N_{Z/X}$.

Define $E(A,I_U)\to(A/I_U)[t]$ by discarding the negative Laurent powers and reducing all remaining coefficients modulo $I_U$. This is multiplicative: a product involving a negative-power coefficient has that coefficient in $I_U$, so if its total exponent is nonnegative its coefficient still vanishes modulo $I_U$; products of nonnegative terms reduce coefficientwise. The map is surjective and sends $a/t$ to zero. Localizing by $S$ gives the surjection $Q(A,I_U)\to(A/I_U)\otimes_kR$, hence a closed immersion $Z_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde X_Z$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Modulo $t$ the map is identity in degree zero and zero in positive associated-graded degrees; thus its special fibre is exactly the zero section specified in [pur9-def-normal-cone]. On a principal restriction the coefficient class $a\bmod I_U$ maps to $a/1\bmod I_UA_s$ and each negative-degree generator still maps to zero. Thus the local morphisms agree on a basis of each overlap and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

Choose a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $X$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] each $A_i$ is Noetherian, hence its ideal $I_i$ has finitely many generators $a_{ij}$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The algebra $Q(A_i,I_i)$ is generated over $R$ by finite algebra generators of $A_i$ and the finite family $a_{ij}/t$. The inverse images of the $U_{i,D}$ form a finite affine cover, so [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives finite type over $D$. The relative-Spec projection is affine, hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). The diagonal of $X_D/D$ is the base change of the closed diagonal of $X/k$, and is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Its part (e) gives separatedness of the composite $\widetilde X_Z\to X_D\to D$. Together with Step 3 this is a separated finite-type lift in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. This calculation was for an arbitrary separated finite-type $k$-scheme and closed ideal: substituting the finite affine algebras and ideal generators of $(X',Z')$, $(C,W)$ or $(F,Z_F)$ proves the lift property for those pairs once their hypotheses have been checked.

source.place: Notation 1.4.1(a)--(b), finiteness/separatedness of the lift; Stacks 00FM (Noetherian ideals), 01T0 (finite type), 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated), 01QR (closed-immersion base change), 01KU (separated compositions)

proof.text: On affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X'$ mapping into $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the $k$-algebra map. Coefficientwise application of $\varphi$ to Laurent polynomials carries $E(A,I_U)$ into $E(B,J_V)$ because $\varphi(I_U)B\subseteq J_V$. It preserves $S$, as $f$ is a $k$-morphism, so it induces $Q(A,I_U)\to Q(B,J_V)$. The affine spectrum functor and the relative-Spec charts give the desired morphism over $f_D$. On a common affine refinement of an overlap, both chart maps send every coefficient to its image under $f^\sharp$, fix $t$ and $S$, and send $a/t$ to $f^\sharp(a)/t$. They therefore agree there and on the overlap; [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them. For uniqueness, any algebra map over $f_D$ must send $a/t$ to the unique solution of $t x=\varphi(a)$; multiplication by $t$ is injective in the subring $Q(B,J_V)\subset B\otimes_k k(t)$. Thus every generator has the required image, proving uniqueness. These same formulas show identity and composition functoriality. Modulo $t$, the degree-$n$ map is $I_U^n/I_U^{n+1}\to J_V^n/J_V^{n+1}$, $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$, as asserted.

source.place: Lemma 1.4.3(a) and the first sentence of its proof of (b); Stacks 01SA and 01JJ/04TN for chartwise maps and gluing

proof.text: For the support criterion put $K=\varphi(I_U)B\subseteq J_V$ and $G=\operatorname{gr}_{J_V}B$. Choose generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $I_U$ as in Step 5, and let $h_i$ be the degree-one class of $\varphi(a_i)$ in $G$. The ideal pulled back from the zero section of $N_{Z/X}$ is generated by the $h_i$: every positive-degree class of $\operatorname{gr}_{I_U}A$ is a sum of products of degree-one classes, since elements of $I_U^n$ are sums of products from $I_U$. If the special-fibre image is supported on the zero section, each $h_i$ vanishes in every residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}G$. Its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3); [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] then makes its underlying space quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qc-scheme-vanishing-section-nilpotent] applies and gives $h_i^{e_i}=0$ for some $e_i\ge1$. Set $r=1+\sum_i(e_i-1)$ (take $r=1$ when the family is empty). Every product of $r$ of the $h_i$ contains some $h_i^{e_i}$, so $(h_1,\ldots,h_s)^r=0$. In homogeneous degree $r$ this says exactly $K^r\subseteq J_V^{r+1}$, including all $B$-linear combinations.

source.place: Lemma 1.4.3(b), expanded nilpotence inference; Stacks 03GY (lemma-stein-universally-closed), proof: a section vanishing everywhere on a quasi-compact scheme is nilpotent

proof.text: Conversely, if $K^r\subseteq J_V^{r+1}$, then every degree-$r$ product of the $h_i$ is zero, hence $h_i^r=0$ for each $i$. At any prime of $G$ its image in the residue field is therefore zero; the special-fibre map has image in the zero-section locus. To obtain a global exponent in the forward direction, cover $X'$ by finitely many affine $V$ mapping into affine $U$ as above: fix the finite affine $U_i$ of Step 5, choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ inside $f^{-1}(U_i)$ at each point of $X'$, and take a finite subcover. The underlying space of $X'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], since $X'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and finite type. Step 7 supplies an exponent on each chart. If $K^r\subseteq J^{r+1}$ then for $N\ge r$ one has $K^N\subseteq K^rJ^{N-r}\subseteq J^{N+1}$ because $K\subseteq J$. The maximum of the finite list of exponents therefore works on every chart, hence as an inclusion of ideal sheaves. The reverse implication is already local. If $X'$ is empty, all inclusions hold with $r=1$ and the image condition is vacuous.

source.place: Lemma 1.4.3(b), globalization of the affine calculation by quasi-compactness and monotonicity of the exponent

proof.text: Assume now $J=f^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_{X'}$, namely $J_V=\varphi(I_U)B$ on the above charts. The affine fibre-product formula identifies the part of $\widetilde X_Z\times_X X'$ over $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AQ(A,I_U))$. Its map to $Q(B,J_V)$ sends $b\otimes q$ to $b\varphi(q)$ and is surjective: coefficients in $B\otimes_kR$ are in its image, and if $j=\sum b_i\varphi(a_i)\in J_V$, then $j/t=\sum b_i\varphi(a_i)/t$ is in its image. The target algebra is generated by these elements. Thus the induced morphism is a closed immersion by the affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The formulas are the coefficient maps of Step 6, so this is precisely the stated canonical comparison, and the affine-chart conclusion gives a global closed immersion. No flatness of $f$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 1.4.3(c); Stacks 01I4/01JQ (affine fibre products), 01QO (affine criterion for a closed immersion)

proof.text: The ideal of the zero section in $\operatorname{gr}_{I_U}A$ is its positive-degree ideal. In $G=\operatorname{gr}_{J_V}B$, its extension contains every degree-one element: $J_V=\varphi(I_U)B$ makes each such class a $B/J_V$-linear combination of images of degree-one classes. All positive-degree elements of $G$ are sums of products of degree-one classes. Hence the extended ideal is exactly $G_{>0}$, with quotient $B/J_V$. This proves scheme-theoretically, not just on points, that the inverse image of the zero section is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J_V)=Z'\cap V$. The affine identifications respect restrictions and so give the asserted equality with $Z'$ globally.

source.place: Lemma 1.4.3(d), direct graded-ideal computation (equivalent to its proof using (c))

proof.text: First check that $(X\times_kX,Z\times_kZ)$ is an allowed pair. The finite affine cover $U_i$ of Step 5 gives the finite affine cover $U_i\times_kU_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_kA_j)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; the tensor algebra is generated over $k$ by $a\otimes1$ and $1\otimes b$ for the chosen finite algebra generators $a,b$, so it is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. After reordering the four factors, the diagonal of $X\times_kX$ is the product of the two diagonals of $X$. Each is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; their product factors as two base changes of closed immersions and hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) and composition of surjective affine ring maps. Thus the product is separated. For the correspondence write $W=c^{-1}(Z\times Z)$ with ideal $L=c_1^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_C+c_2^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_C$. The ideal of $Z\times Z$ is generated by the two pulled-back ideals: on an affine product the quotient by their sum is $(A/I_U)\otimes_k(A'/I_{U'})$, by the affine fibre-product formula. Thus this is the scheme-theoretic inverse image required by the statement. Step 6 applied to the two maps of pairs $(C,W)\to(X,Z)$ constructs $\widetilde c_1,\widetilde c_2$, and their common $D$-structure gives $\widetilde c=(\widetilde c_1,\widetilde c_2)$ into $\widetilde X_Z\times_D\widetilde X_Z$ by the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product]. This is also the map obtained by first lifting $c$ to the deformation of $(X\times X,Z\times Z)$ and then lifting the two projections: Step 6's composition formula sends each generator $a/t$ to the same pulled-back element. Thus the construction in §1.4.4 gives exactly the displayed lifted correspondence without needing an unproved assertion that arbitrary Rees base change is an isomorphism.

source.place: §1.4.4; Lemma 1.4.3(a) applied to the legs and the projections of the product

proof.text: Let $i_F:F\to C$ and $d:F\to X$ be the fixed projections. By [def-trf-fixed-scheme], $c_1i_F=d=c_2i_F$ and $F$ is the base change of the diagonal. Since $X/k$ is separated, that diagonal is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $i_F$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). For a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $C$, the inverse images in $F$ are $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i/H_i)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the images of finite $k$-algebra generators of $B_i$ generate the quotients, giving finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The immersion $i_F$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; part (e) of the permanence node and separatedness of $C/k$ give separatedness of $F/k$. Therefore Step 5 applies to $(F,Z_F)$. Pulling $L$ back to $F$ gives $d^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_F+d^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_F=d^{-1}I\,\mathcal O_F$, which is the ideal of $Z_F=d^{-1}Z$. Consequently $Z_F=i_F^{-1}W$ scheme-theoretically. Step 9 applied to $i_F$ gives a closed immersion $\widetilde F_{Z_F}\to\widetilde C_W\times_C F$. The latter projects to $\widetilde C_W$ by a base change of the closed immersion $i_F$. Their composite is closed: on affine charts both maps are surjective ring maps and their composite is surjective, so [def-weil-closed-immersion] applies.

source.place: Corollary 1.4.5, first sentence of the proof; Lemma 1.4.3(c),(e); Stacks 01QR (base change of closed immersions), 01QO (affine criterion)

proof.text: The two maps $\widetilde F_{Z_F}\to\widetilde X_Z$ obtained by composing with the lifted legs are equal: by Step 6's composition formula both are the lift of $d:(F,Z_F)\to(X,Z)$. Therefore the composite in Step 12 factors through the fibre product $\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$ with the relative diagonal, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The relative diagonal is closed because Step 5 proved $\widetilde X_Z/D$ separated, so $\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)\to\widetilde C_W$ is closed by closed-immersion base change. Both the Step 12 map and this map are closed immersions into the same scheme. The factor is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion]: on an affine ambient chart the two surjections have kernels $K$ and $H$, factorization says $H\subseteq K$, and the factor is $Q/H\twoheadrightarrow Q/K$. Thus the required fixed-scheme inclusion is scheme-theoretic and natural in the original pair and correspondence.

source.place: Corollary 1.4.5, second sentence of the proof; Stacks 01QP (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals), 01QR (closed-immersion base change)

proof.text: Finally Step 3 identifies all generic-fibre spaces with their original spaces base changed to $\eta$, and Step 6 identifies the maps with $c_{i,\eta},i_{F,\eta},d_\eta$. Fibre-product universality then identifies $\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)_\eta$ with $C_\eta\times_{X_\eta\times_\eta X_\eta}X_\eta=F_\eta$. The generic fibre of the constructed immersion has projections $i_{F,\eta}$ and $d_\eta$, so under this identification it is the identity of $F_\eta$. This is the canonical generic-fibre identification claimed, including the case of an empty fixed scheme.

Under J=IB the tensor map is surjective via j/t = sum b_i phi(a_i)/t, so it is a closed immersion. The extended gr_{>0} equals G_{>0}, so the inverse image is B/J scheme-theoretically. The ideal of W is c1.I+c2.I, which pulls back to d.I on F, so Z_F = i_F^{-1}W. The two lifted composites agree by Step 6.
